hello.note: Same Perso-Arabic word as Persian salam; used the same way across Iranian Azerbaijan (Tabriz, Urmia).

good_morning.note: Literally 'may your morning be good'; the native Turkic greeting. Many Tabrizis just say the Persian sobh bekheyr instead.

goodbye.note: Literally 'stay healthy'; the everyday informal goodbye. Xudahafiz (خداحافظ), borrowed straight from Persian, is just as common in Iranian Azerbaijani speech.

how_are_you.note: Polite/plural form. With close friends people often ask Nə var, nə yox? (نه وار، نه یوخ؛ 'what's up, what's not').

thank_you.note: Standard thank you. Çox sağ ol (چوخ ساغ اول, 'be very healthy') is the everyday casual version.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'please, go ahead'; a warm, general-purpose courtesy word also used as a reply to thanks, like Turkish buyurun.

no_problem.note: Literally 'it doesn't touch/matter'; the casual brush-off for small favors, distinct from the more formal buyurun.

sorry.note: Bağışlayın (excuse me) also doubles as a lighter sorry.

yes.note: Casual hə (هه) is very common in fast speech.

of_course.note: Shared with Persian albatteh; enthusiastic agreement to do something.

cheers.note: Said when raising a glass; literally 'to your health'.
